elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor or otherwise burdening Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause is intentionally omitted, so it imposes no MFN obligation on Customer.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer is limited to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation remains, so the condition requiring a defined-product limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer applies for no more than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation remains, so the condition requiring a 12-month limit is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any MFN obligation burdening Customer includes reasonable carve-outs excluding non-comparable terms, suppliers, transactions, or circumstances.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation remains, so the condition requiring reasonable-comparison carve-outs is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: Deleting clause 7.2 fully achieves the preferred position and, as the more protective outcome, also satisfies each conditional fallback limitation because no Customer MFN obligation remains. The change is confined to the targeted MFN clause and introduces no contradiction. “Intentionally omitted” is operative and clear, although retaining the numbering is mainly administrative.
